name: Sweet and Sour Sheet-Pan Chicken

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to about 6 inches from heat source. Place a large rimmed baking sheet on rack and preheat oven to 450°F. In a large bowl, toss chicken, bell peppers, onion, oil, kosher salt, and black pepper until evenly coated. Remove baking sheet from oven. Carefully spread chicken mixture in an even layer on baking sheet. Return baking sheet to oven and roast until chicken and vegetables begin to brown, 10 to 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, whisk apricot preserves, vinegar, ketchup, soy sauce, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic until smooth. Transfer 1/2 cup glaze to a small saucepan and set aside.

Once chicken and vegetables begin to brown, remove baking sheet from oven and add sugar snap peas and remaining glaze in the bowl to chicken mixture; toss until evenly coated, then spread into an even layer. Set oven to broil. Broil until chicken is browned and registers at least 175°F on an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest portion and sugar snap peas are crisp-tender, 3 to 5 minutes.
While chicken broils, bring reserved glaze in saucepan to a simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring often, until slightly thickened and glossy, about 3 minutes. Remove saucepan from heat.
Brush all but 2 tablespoons thickened glaze over chicken and vegetables. Return baking sheet to oven and broil until glaze is caramelized, 1 to 2 minutes.
Serve with rice, drizzling individual portions with remaining thickened glaze. Top with scallions, if desired.

description: This easy sweet-and-sour sheet-pan chicken pairs juicy chicken thighs, crisp vegetables, and a glossy apricot glaze for a fast, flavorful dinner.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Steamed white rice, for serving; Thinly sliced scallions, for serving (optional)

Optional substitutions: red bell peppers → orange bell peppers

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Laila Ibrahim
